content: The document outlines detailed guidelines for monitoring and reporting key HIV-related indicators in healthcare facilities. 1. Antiretroviral Therapy (ART) Reporting: Facilities must track the cumulative number of individuals who have ever started ART by the end of the previous reporting period. This includes disaggregating data by sex (males and females over 14 years) and age (boys and girls aged 0–14 years). New individuals who started ART during the current reporting period must also be recorded. These numbers are added to the cumulative total to determine the updated cumulative figure at the end of the current reporting period. The percentage of males, females, boys, and girls on ART is calculated by dividing the respective group totals by the overall total and multiplying by 100. 2. ART Regimen Monitoring: The ART register is used to document the number of individuals on first-line, second-line, and third-line ART regimens at the end of the reporting period. This data is further categorized by age groups (adults ≥15 years and children 0–14 years) and sex. Even if a patient switches regimens during the reporting period, only the regimen recorded at the end of the period is counted. 3. Antenatal Care (ANC) and HIV Testing: The ANC register is used to report on all pregnant women enrolled in ANC during the reporting period. This includes: Women known to be HIV-positive at the time of enrollment. Women tested for HIV during ANC and their results (HIV-positive or HIV-negative). The total number of HIV-positive pregnant women (both known and newly diagnosed) is calculated, along with the percentage of those who started ART either before or during ANC. 4. Labour and Delivery (L&D) HIV Testing: For women delivering at the facility, the report includes: Those known to be HIV-positive at arrival. Those with unknown HIV status who were tested during L&D and received their results. The number of women who tested HIV-positive during L&D. The total number of HIV-positive women on ART during L&D is also recorded, ensuring reconciliation with ANC data to avoid double-counting. 5. HIV-Exposed Infants (HEI): The HEI register tracks all HIV-exposed infants born within the past 12 months. Key indicators include: The number of infants started on antiretroviral prophylaxis at birth. The number who received an HIV virological test by two months of age. The number started on cotrimoxazole (CTX) prophylaxis by two months of age. 6. Data Collection and Tallying: At the end of each reporting period (monthly or quarterly, depending on the country’s system), data from the ART, ANC, and L&D registers are tallied and recorded in a cross-sectional report. This report provides a snapshot of key indicators at a specific point in time. one to read out the data and the other to record and categorize it by sex, age, and pregnancy status. 7. Avoiding Double-Counting: Transfer-in patients (those who started ART at another facility) should not be included in the cumulative total of individuals ever started on ART at the current facility. ANC and L&D registers must be reconciled to prevent double-counting of women already tested and on ART during ANC. 8. Viral Load and TB Monitoring: Viral load results recorded in the past 12 months are tracked, including the number of individuals with suppressed viral loads. ART coverage during TB treatment is also monitored, ensuring integration of HIV and TB care. These guidelines aim to standardize the collection and reporting of HIV-related data, ensuring accurate monitoring of treatment coverage, testing, and outcomes for both adults and children.
